To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MIST1 and the pancreatic basic helix-loop–helix transcription factor PTF1 collaborate in extensive feed-forward regulatory loops that maintain the differentiated phenotype of pancreatic acinar secretory cells.
the MIST1 and pancreatic transcription factor PTF1 collaborate in feed-forward regulatory loops that maintain the differentiated phenotype of pancreatic acinar cell.
the transcription factors MIST 1 and PTF 1 collaborate in a feed forward regulatory loop to maintain the differentiated phenotype of pancreatic acinar epithelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptional control of the differentiated state of the adult pancreatic secretory acinar cell and the regulatory networks that govern it.
the regulatory networks of transcription factors in differentiated mammalian cells.
the regulatory networks that govern the maintenance of the specialized acinar cell phenotype and the role of transcription factors in the regulation of gene transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MIST1-PTF1 collaboration is essential for the maintenance of the differentiated pancreatic acinar cell phenotype in adult mice.
PTF1 and the MIST1 transcription factors form feed-forward loops that are critical to the maintenance of pancreatic acinar cell function in adult mice.
the transcription factors PTF1 and Mist1 collaborate to form an extensive feed-forward regulatory loop that maintains the acinar cell phenotype in adult mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PTF1-MIST1 regulatory network maintains the specialized pancreatic acinar cell phenotype by driving the transcription of hundreds of genes that control a broad spectrum of cellular processes.
PTF1 and Mist1 form a feed-forward loop that is essential for maintenance of the pancreatic acinar phenotype.
PTF1 and Mist1 form a feed-forward regulatory loop that maintains the differentiated acinar cell phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional networks that govern the mature, differentiated phenotype of a mammalian cell type in vivo can be complex.
transcription factors can form extensive regulatory networks in vivo that control the differentiation and maintenance of the differentiated state of mature, specialized cells.
the MIST1 and the PTF1 collaboration is a major regulatory force in adult pancreatic acinar cells.
